cards.name: rank-levers-by-energy-removed-once-the-power-cap-binds-e2e-gfx942-compute-bound
cards.description: Power-capped fp8 block-scale MoE GEMM pair, gfx942: scalar-FMA rescale, VALU strip, padding-MFMA skip, 2-kernel sort paid +6.3%; L2-miss cuts did not
cards.key: fp8 block-scale (128x128 weight, 1x128 activation) two-stage fused-MoE GEMM pair in FlyDSL on gfx942/MI300X, MFMA-bound against a binding socket power cap, after the native-fp8 rewrite to 2 waves/SIMD has landed
cards.effect: 1.62x geomean vs the frozen vendor baseline, director-verified (per-case 1.58x at 2048 and 1.67x at 4096 tokens per rank); this lane added +6.3% (per-case +5.7% / +6.9%, cross-session) over a warm-started two-stage at 1.53x, each landed step winning 86-100% of its interleaved same-session paired rounds
cards.roofline: fp8-MFMA-bound at a binding socket power cap before and after, sustained clock about half of max; first-GEMM MFMA-busy 61-66% -> 65-74% and issue-wait 56% -> 49%; EA traffic 35-40% of peak; 2 waves/SIMD throughout; cutting 9.5-9.9% of cycles per forward bought only 3.4-3.9% of time, so time tracks energy per forward
cards.title: Rank levers by energy removed once the power cap binds
cards.lever: Once an fp8 block-scale MoE GEMM pair is MFMA-bound against a binding socket power cap, time per forward tracks energy per forward, so rank candidates by the energy they remove: removed MFMA work, HBM bytes and memory-side atomics converted about 1:1; letting the first GEMM issue MFMAs more densely converted about 45%; pure stall or nop cuts and L2 misses the device-wide cache already served converted about 0. The largest single step on gfx942 was emitting the per-K-block fp32 rescale as per-element scalar FMAs, because packed-FP32 VALU waits for the MFMA pipe to drain while two scalar FMAs co-issue almost free.
cards.apply: Scalar rescale = one llvm.fma per accumulator element inside the K loop (packed FP32 outside it measured neutral), plus waves_per_eu=2 to hold 2 waves/SIMD; setprio wraps the whole K loop; in the second GEMM a per-column-block scale-product table in LDS turns the rescale into one bare FMA and absorbs the routing weight; the sort writes a valid-row count per M block that each GEMM s_loads to branch uniformly to a full, 2-subtile or 1-subtile body; a 2-kernel count/place sort owns the zero-fill and strides every loop by its own grid.
cards.stack:
total 1.62x vs the frozen vendor baseline (director-verified); about 1.53x of it is the warm-started native-fp8 rewrite (covered separately) and +6.3% came from four directions over two rounds
  - 1. second-GEMM VALU strip under whole-K-loop setprio (scale-product table, folded routing weight, leaner epilogue, 1 VALU per MFMA slot): +1.82% same-session (round 2, verified)
  - 2. 2-kernel count/place sort owning the zero-fill, 6 -> 4 dispatches: +0.65% alone, +0.61-0.70% on top of (1) (round 2, verified)
  - 3. first-GEMM per-element scalar-FMA rescale (+2.30% alone), then a maxnum row-max epilogue and whole-K-loop setprio: +2.78% same-session (round 3, verified)
  - 4. sort-emitted valid-row count driving an all-padding-subtile skip: second GEMM +0.71% (verified), +0.61% on top of (3); the first-GEMM skip added +0.31% (round 3, integrated)
  - note: incremental in landing order; rounds compare across sessions (~1% drift). A later stack (single-expert rows as plain stores + multi-row-only fill, second-GEMM scalar rescale, skip repair) verified +1.76-1.92% same-session but is outside the total: it missed the +2% commit gate by 0.14%
cards.verify: Check engagement in the ISA before timing (no v_pk_fma_f32 inside the MFMA loop, one scalar FMA per MFMA, 0 spills at 2 waves/SIMD, full-body ISA unchanged by the skip variants) and in the trace (both GEMMs by name, dispatch count); then time the whole forward: 12-30 interleaved paired rounds with rotating arm order, pooled over 2-4 GPUs with a null arm, every arm from a frozen source snapshot because the DSL traces source at first call.
cards.pitfall:
An earlier steer to pack the rescale into v_pk_fma_f32 was inverted: the fully scalar form made the GEMM 3.5-3.8% faster → on gfx942 packed FP32 waits for the matrix pipe to drain (an MFMA + pk-FMA pair costs ~1.8x the cycles of MFMA + 2 scalar FMAs) and LLVM unpacks FP32 inside MFMA shadows on purpose → micro-bench the co-issue pair first, then emit scalar FMAs
- pitfall: The same swap in the second GEMM cut that kernel 1.6-1.9% but the forward only ~0.2%, and an isolated first-GEMM A/B overstated its forward gain ~2x → under the cap the next kernel inherits the lower clock → judge every kernel change at the forward level
- pitfall: Moving the scale product into LDS lost 16% → it pushed the second GEMM to 272 VGPR and 1 wave/SIMD → pin waves_per_eu=2 in the same change
- pitfall: Per-tile s_setprio lost ~5% → setprio is a scheduling-region boundary that cuts each tile's sched_group_barrier pattern off its MFMAs → wrap the whole K loop once
- pitfall: The first-GEMM padding skip cut MFMA rows 3.5% / 1.9% but returned only 20-30% of that → early-exiting tail CTAs desync their same-weight-panel siblings in the one-shot grid (+16% / +8% L2 misses) and the variant bodies spilled → a per-variant prologue (0 spills) plus short s_sleep tail pacing cut the L2-miss excess by a third to a half (+0.25-0.36% forward); variant sets other than 4,2,1 perturbed the full body's register allocation
- pitfall: CTA reorders that cut first-GEMM L2 misses by up to a quarter returned at most +0.27%, or lost 1.4% behind a dependent remap prologue → the removed misses were cross-XCD re-fetches the device-wide Infinity Cache already served, while sibling-CTA weight-panel sharing is load-bearing (non-temporal weight loads cost 20-24%) → count bytes at HBM, not L2 misses
cards.caution: Also verify that the power cap actually binds (sustained socket power at the limit, clock far below max) before ranking by energy, since unthrottled stall cuts should convert normally; and also verify the target has no scaled-MFMA path for the block scales before porting the scalar-FMA step (on gfx942 one scalar FMA per MFMA was irreducible).
